key_insight: Machine learning on EHR data can accurately infer several family relationship types, especially when training is focused on records with shared contact information.
clinical_relevance: Automatically identifying family links in health records could improve patient-centered research and healthcare workflows, but only for relationships that are detectable from existing data.
method: Random Forest classifiers for Mother-Child, Father-Child, Sibling-Sibling, Twin-Twin, and Partner-Partner relationships
Four-stage refinement: initial training, multicollinearity reduction, feature engineering, and training-data refinement
Used INPC EHR data plus Indiana Natality records as the gold standard, with negative pairs selected through blocking and similarity filters
evidence_signal: Across the five relationship types, the models reached precision of 0.92-1.00, recall of 0.97-1.00, and F1 of 0.94-1.00 in large-scale evaluation.
watch_item: A substantial share of true relationships had no shared contact information in EHRs, making them structurally undetectable and limiting real-world coverage.
paper_title: Identifying Family Relationships from Electronic Health Records: A Machine Learning Approach
